```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
options("giotto.use_conda" = FALSE, "giotto.no_python_warn" = TRUE)
```

A `giotto` object is large, deeply nested, and mostly opaque from the console.
Two questions come up constantly and neither has a good answer from printed
output:

* **What is in this object?**
* **Did the step I just ran actually change anything?**

`objManifest()` answers the first and `manifestDiff()` answers the second.

```{r, message = FALSE}
library(GiottoClass)

g <- GiottoData::loadGiottoMini("vizgen")
activeSpatUnit(g) <- "aggregate"

objManifest(g)
```

The manifest is what the object **is**. Its companion, `objHistory()`, records
**why** it looks that way. The two are deliberately separate: the history is
provenance, and object state is never reconstructed by replaying it.

## Reading the inventory

`slots` holds one entry per non-empty slot, and each entry is a list of
records, one per subobject. A record's identity is under `keys`: the accessor
arguments that retrieve it, and only the ones that apply. Everything else
describes it: its class, its form, and a fingerprint of its content.

```{r}
m <- objManifest(g)
str(m$slots$expression[[1]])
```

Because the keys are the getter's own arguments, a record maps straight onto a
call:

```{r}
rec <- m$slots$dimension_reduction[[1]]
rec$keys

pca <- do.call(getDimReduction, c(list(g), rec$keys, list(output = "dimObj")))
objName(pca)
```

Records report form and content, not size. Dimensions, row counts and extents
are deliberately absent: on a disk-backed object each one costs a scan of the
data. The counts that matter for reading a diff are in the `summary` block,
which comes from the object's id slots for free:

```{r}
unlist(m$summary$n_cells)
```

Every field is read through its own guard. A field that cannot be read becomes
`NULL` and its path is listed in `warnings`, rather than erroring the whole
manifest: a state report that crashes is worse than no state report. On a
healthy object the list is empty:

```{r}
m$warnings
```

## Did my step do anything?

This is the day-to-day use. Take a manifest before the step, another after,
and ask what moved:

```{r}
before <- objManifest(g)

g <- createSpatialNetwork(g, name = "tutorial_net", method = "Delaunay")

manifestDiff(before, objManifest(g))$summary
```

Steps that overwrite something already present are the interesting case.
Recomputing an existing network leaves its name and its place untouched, and
only the content changes. The fingerprint is what sees it:

```{r}
before <- objManifest(g)

g <- createNearestNetwork(g, name = "sNN.pca", k = 10)

manifestDiff(before, objManifest(g))$summary
```

A step that changes the cells changes nearly everything at once. The count
change is stated once and the records that moved with it are tallied, rather
than listed one by one:

```{r}
gs <- subsetGiotto(g, cell_ids = head(spatIDs(g), 100))
manifestDiff(objManifest(g), objManifest(gs))$summary
```

`manifestDiff()` also returns `changed` (a flag) and `detail` (every affected
record, as data). The one-sentence `summary` is what you would hand to a
person, or a model; `detail` is what you would score or assert against.

## Fingerprints

Every record carries a fingerprint: a short hash that changes when the content
changes. Cell metadata goes one step further and fingerprints each column, so
a diff names the column an edit touched, even an edit to a single cell that
leaves the column's levels unchanged:

```{r}
before <- objManifest(g)

cm <- getCellMetadata(g, output = "cellMetaObj")
lv <- unique(cm[]$leiden_clus)
cm[]$leiden_clus[1] <- setdiff(lv, cm[]$leiden_clus[1])[[1]]
g_edit <- setGiotto(g, cm, verbose = FALSE)

manifestDiff(before, objManifest(g_edit))$summary
```

Level counts are not reported by default: counting the distinct values of
every column is a full pass over the table, and the fingerprints already say
which column changed. Ask for them with `levels = TRUE` and the diff says what
a re-clustering produced:

```{r}
cm2 <- getCellMetadata(g, output = "cellMetaObj")
cm2[]$leiden_clus <- cm2[]$leiden_clus %% 3
g_regroup <- setGiotto(g, cm2, verbose = FALSE)

manifestDiff(objManifest(g, levels = TRUE),
             objManifest(g_regroup, levels = TRUE))$summary
```

How a fingerprint is computed depends on what the subobject holds:

| Payload | Fingerprinted from |
|---|---|
| matrices, tables, graphs, view and space steps | all of their values, exactly |
| polygons and points | a fixed-stride sample of the geometries and their attributes, plus the overall extent |
| images | the pixels read at display resolution, plus extent |
| disk-backed stores | the store's handle: its identity, recorded operations and schema |
| BPCells and HDF5Array matrices | their delayed operations, and the names and sizes of their backing files |
| functions | their code; values a closure captures are not seen |

A fingerprint is never a hash of the R object itself. Objects that hold an
external pointer or an environment hash differently every time they are
created, even when their content is identical; a fingerprint is built from the
content extracted out of them. It is deterministic and never touches the RNG.

It costs little. In-memory content of half a million cells hashes in a few tens
of milliseconds, and an image costs the same whatever its size.

Two comparisons are deliberately loose. Geometry coordinates are compared as a
set of vertices to 12 significant digits, because writing a polygon to a
shapefile and reading it back reorders its vertices and drops the last bits of
a double. And images are read at display resolution, which uses a file's
overviews when it has them; so the same pixels saved in a format with
overviews, such as a COG, fingerprint differently once.

Payloads GiottoClass does not know get their fingerprint from the package that
provides them, through the `fingerprint_data()` generic. A payload with no
method has no fingerprint, and the manifest says so in `warnings`. The diff
says so too, instead of claiming nothing changed:

```{r}
gu <- g
e <- gu@expression$aggregate$rna$raw
e@exprMat <- structure(list(), class = "someNewFormat")
gu@expression$aggregate$rna$raw <- e

mu <- objManifest(gu)
mu$warnings
manifestDiff(mu, objManifest(gu))$summary
```

## The history log

`objHistory()` returns the object's history as one record per step:

```{r}
g <- subsetGiotto(g, cell_ids = head(spatIDs(g), 100))

str(tail(objHistory(g), 1)[[1]], max.level = 1)
```

`params` holds the arguments the function actually ran with, as deparsed
expressions, so `1:30` survives as `"1:30"`.

Not every change is logged, though. Only a minority of the suite's functions
call `update_giotto_params()`, and a direct slot assignment calls nothing at
all, so an object's contents can move with nothing in its history claiming
responsibility. `recordGiottoStep()` closes that gap for a caller that can see
the change happen:

```{r}
before <- objManifest(g)

cm <- getCellMetadata(g, output = "cellMetaObj")
cm[]$hand_label <- rep(c("tumor", "stroma"), length.out = nrow(cm))
g <- setGiotto(g, cm, verbose = FALSE)

d <- manifestDiff(before, objManifest(g))
d$summary

g <- recordGiottoStep(g, fn = "manual annotation",
                      status = "unattributed", diff = d$detail)

tail(names(objHistory(g)), 1)
```

A failed call is recordable the same way, with `status = "error"`.

## On disk

`saveGiotto()` writes two sidecars beside the object: `manifest.json` (what it
is) and `history.ndjson` (why, one operation per line).

```{r}
td <- file.path(tempdir(), "manifest_vignette")
dir.create(td, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

saveGiotto(g, dir = td, foldername = "mini", verbose = FALSE)

saved <- file.path(td, "mini")
list.files(saved)
```

The point of the sidecar is that it answers questions about the object without
loading it. `objManifest()` reads it back from the folder, in the same form it
returns for a live object:

```{r, eval = requireNamespace("jsonlite", quietly = TRUE)}
ms <- objManifest(saved)
unlist(ms$summary$n_cells)
```

So a saved object can be diffed against a live one, or against another save,
without loading either. Fingerprints survive the round trip, so the diff
reports only what changed since the save:

```{r, eval = requireNamespace("jsonlite", quietly = TRUE)}
g_after <- createSpatialNetwork(g, name = "after_save", method = "Delaunay")
manifestDiff(ms, objManifest(g_after))$summary
```

`objManifest(output = "json")` returns the same document for any object as a
string, and `objManifest(file = )` writes it. `objHistory()` takes the same
`output = "ndjson"` and `file` for the history, and reads `history.ndjson`
back from the folder the same way. The JSON follows a versioned schema that ships with the
package:

```{r}
system.file("schema", "giotto-manifest-0.2.0.json", package = "GiottoClass")
```

Records are sorted by their keys so two manifests of the same state serialize
identically, and `NA`, `NaN` and `Inf` are encoded as strings so that a missing
value stays distinguishable from a not-a-number.

## What it is good for

* Checking that a step did what you expected, and noticing when it did
  nothing.
* Inspecting a saved object without loading it.
* Regression-testing a pipeline: same inputs should give the same fingerprints.
* Diffing two runs, or the same analysis before and after a parameter change.
* Turning `history.ndjson` into a methods section.
* Giving an assistant, an eval harness or a reviewer machine-readable state
  instead of printed text.

## What it does not do

* **Sizes are not reported.** Dimensions, row counts and extents would each
  cost a scan on a disk-backed object, so records carry none; the summary
  block's cell and feature counts are the exception.
* **Sampled payloads can miss a local edit.** Moving one polygon that falls
  outside the geometry sample, or painting a few pixels between the points an
  image is read at, can leave the fingerprint unchanged. Matrices, tables and
  graphs are hashed in full and have no such gap.
* **Disk-backed payloads need a method.** A store is fingerprinted only once
  the package that provides it implements `fingerprint_data()`. Until then it
  is listed in `warnings` and the diff counts it as unfingerprinted.
* **The history is not complete by construction.** It records what functions
  chose to log. Entries written with `toplevel = 1` name
  `update_giotto_params` rather than the calling function, a property of those
  call sites, not of the record.
* **The schema is 0.2.0 and not yet released.** Treat the field set as stable
  in spirit, not frozen.
